dataset: AI clauses in US court protective and confidentiality orders, coded for how they treat a self-hosted open-weight model (frame: E-Discovery LLC blog posts, 1 Oct 2025 - 31 Oct 2026)
maintainer: MV2 of Munim, Inc. (mv2@munimtech.com); coded with AI agents working in his name
license: CC BY 4.0 for the coding; quoted court text is public record; blog posts are not reproduced
status_note: Final coding of 2 November 2026, frozen and published before any count or prediction was computed. Since 0.9.2: Fischman is coded from the protective order itself (ECF 58, read free at the source); Dunn is final as not codable (the free order granting the motion describes the agreed AI provision but does not set out its words, and the protective order is PACER-only); Velez is recoded from its five provisos, now copied in full from the PDF (R13). No case is pending.
coding_rules: R1 (pre-registered unit). One case per court case; if a case has several AI orders in the frame, the latest is used. When the same order is quoted in several posts, the copy in the latest post is used.

R2. 'Quoted' means the order's own words appear in the post, as a block quote or in quotation marks. A court's later summary of an order, a parenthetical description, or a post saying that an order is 'the same' as another is not a quotation; such cases are not codable unless the order can be read free at the source.

R3. A span must point to the order's own words with a start anchor that occurs once in the post. Where an order's quoted text is word for word a part of another order's quotation in the same post, no span can point to it alone, and the case is listed as not codable with that reason.

R4. Self-hosting named (item 2) requires the words self-hosted, on-premises, locally run or locally installed, or words about a party's own infrastructure or environment. The definition phrase 'whether cloud-based or otherwise' does not count. The result is also reported with it counted (sensitivity 'cloud').

R5 (rule provider_contract). When the only route to use is a contract or commitment binding an outside AI provider or vendor, or an enterprise or commercial subscription, setup A (which has no outside provider) is coded unclear. The result is also reported with these cases coded forbidden.

R6 (rule public_model). 'Publicly accessible' or 'publicly available' attached to a version, service, tool or platform is read as describing the running service that receives the data; setup A's is reachable only from the party's own network. Attached to a model or LLM itself, setup A is coded unclear, because an openly published model is itself publicly available. The result is also reported with these cases coded permitted.
R7. A route through the producing party's consent, the parties' agreement, notice or a court order makes setup A conditional, not forbidden.
R8 (rule open_use_conditions). Where an order lets 'open' systems be used on conditions about disclosure and bars some materials outright, setup A is coded unclear. Also reported as permitted.

R9 (rule provisos_not_copied). Where an order names self-hosted models as permitted subject to provisos that were not copied, setup A is coded unclear until the provisos are read. Also reported as permitted.

Rules R2-R9 were written while coding, after the frame was read; the pre-registration did not fix them. Each rule's cases are marked, and the predictions are reported under the opposite reading as well.

R10. An order the posts describe without quoting is coded from its own text when a free copy is in the RECAP archive (the pre-registration counts an order as not codable only if it also cannot be read free at the source). Its spans point to src:<case_id>, the text pypdf 5.1.0 extracted from that PDF with only CM/ECF page-header stamps and bare page-number lines removed; extraction artefacts (split words, stray date stamps) are left as they are, and quotations skip them with '...'. Where pypdf returns a passage out of page order, the passage is given as two spans in reading order.

R11. An order whose free RECAP copy has no usable text layer (pypdf returns only the CM/ECF stamp, or unreadable characters) is coded from OCR text: pages rendered at 300 dpi grayscale by pdftoppm and read by tesseract 5.5.0 (language eng, page segmentation mode 6), with only well-formed CM/ECF page-header stamps and bare page-number lines removed. The OCR text is not corrected by hand; quotations skip OCR errors (stray '|' marks, misread stamps) with '...'. Its spans point to src:<case_id>, the published OCR text.

R12 (rule own_systems_exclusion). Where an order's definition of an AI tool leaves out software that operates entirely on systems the party controls with no material sent to any third party, setup A (run on a party-controlled server, no outside provider) is outside the clause and is coded permitted, and self-hosting is named. Written while coding, after the frame was read.

R13 (rule self_hosted_contract_proviso). Where an order names self-hosted systems among those permitted but one of its provisos asks for a contract or contractual commitment, which setup A (no outside provider) has no one to give, setup A is coded unclear. The result is also reported with these cases coded permitted. Written while coding, after the frame was read.

cases.note: R10. Use without the producing party's permission is barred only where commercially reasonable efforts to ensure the two safeguards were not taken, so a tool meeting them needs no permission. Names Meta LLAMA, an openly published model, among example tools the safeguards apply to, without making openness a test; the parties' enterprise ChatGPT and Harvey accounts are deemed to satisfy the safeguards. pypdf returns the end of section 13.4 after section 14, so the passage is two spans in reading order.
